Good morning, Bakersfield. It’s Wednesday, August 26, 2026, and we’re looking at a sunny day with a high near 102° and air quality at moderate levels. Overnight, a resident on South M Street had a scare when an unknown subject tried to enter his apartment for a fourth time, prompting him to barricade himself in his bathroom with his dog. Police also handled a brief search for a juvenile who fled in a vehicle and staged for a mental-health crisis on University Avenue. Today’s top story: the California City Council denied two appeals challenging the CoreCivic ICE detention facility’s approvals. Let’s get you caught up on the news, the night, and the week ahead.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity was light and largely quiet across the county, with the most significant call a persistent intruder report that sent a South M Street resident to barricade himself in his bathroom. Around 9:18 p.m., an unknown subject was reported attempting a fourth entry into an apartment on the 2400 block of South M Street, prompting the resident to barricade himself in a bathroom with his dog while officers responded. Elsewhere, at 10:17 p.m., a juvenile fled in a vehicle in Bakersfield; a family member followed but had not yet provided a direction of travel or a description of the vehicle. Early this morning, at 5:09 a.m., police staged for a subject experiencing a mental-health crisis on the 2800 block of University Avenue. No major incidents were reported elsewhere.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 102° and a low around 75° tonight. It’s currently 75° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts are in effect for Kern County. Air quality is 75 — moderate. 

## Top stories

**23ABC reports that the California City Council denied two appeals Tuesday night challenging the approval of the CoreCivic ICE detention facility, allowing the city's existing site plan review and CoreCivic's business license to stand.** The appellants — the Immigrant Legal Resource Center and the Dignity Not Detention Coalition — argued immigration detention is not the same as a prison or correctional facility and is not a permitted use under the city's zoning code. They also argued CoreCivic began operating the facility in August 2025, before the city issued its business license in February 2026, and that the city should have required a new conditional use permit. CoreCivic's attorney, appearing over Zoom, argued the city code does not prohibit the use of the facility as an immigration facility and that it is permitted as a conditional use. The council voted 4-1 to deny both appeals.

**Bakersfield Now tells us that Kern County Sheriff Donny Youngblood will retire in January 2027 after 20 years as sheriff.** Sheriff Youngblood, who has served as the county’s top law enforcement officer since 2006, announced his plans to step down next year. His retirement will mark the end of a long career in Kern County law enforcement, and the search for his successor will begin in the coming months.

**23ABC shares the tragic news that a 16-year-old teen drowned at Lake Ming Tuesday afternoon.** Details are scarce, but the Kern County Sheriff's office says it happened at around 4:50 pm. The 16-year-old went under, and four to five others jumped in the lake to try and save him, but could not find him. A search and rescue team found the teen at around 7 pm. The case is under investigation, and the name of the victim has not yet been released.

## Something good

The Kern County Museum is considering new exhibits that would celebrate local history and culture, including a tribute to country music legend Buck Owens and an oil derrick display. These potential additions would highlight the rich heritage of our community, from the oil industry that shaped our economy to the music that put Bakersfield on the map.

## Coming up this week

This week, there are several public meetings and events worth noting. On Wednesday, August 26, a Special City Council Meeting will take place at 12:00 p.m., followed by a City Council Meeting at 3:30 p.m. and another City Council Meeting at 5:15 p.m. On Thursday, September 2, the Personnel and Processes Committee will meet at 12:00 p.m. Meanwhile, the Fox Theater has a busy lineup of shows starting Tuesday, August 24, with the Cults & Classics: Season Pass 2026-2027. On Friday, August 27, Rodney Carrington will perform, followed by CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE on Saturday, August 28. Willie Barcena takes the stage on Sunday, August 29, along with Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix. Finally, on Saturday, September 4, the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA will be held at the Fox Theater.
